name: deck_find
description: Find text across the deck's words, in every state (PLAN 2.47, 2.83): its texts, each node's description (`alt`), each state's notes, and each beat's claim and notes (`kind`), once for each place they are written (the node's own, a state's delta, the deck's overrides, a state, or a beat), with the states that show them from there and each match, in characters. With `replace`, every match is replaced in one patch, a `replace_text` where each text lives and a JSON Patch `replace` of the rest where they are written, reported as `deck_patch` reports a patch (`replaced`).

bundle.description: The bundle: a directory, a `.scaena` zip, or a `deck.json`.

case.description: Upper and lower case apart; alike without it.

words.description: Whole words only: a match that neither begins nor ends inside a word.

replace.description: Replace every match with this, in one patch: a `replace_text` where each text lives.

dry_run.description: With `replace`: say what would change, and write nothing.

Found.description: Words the deck holds, as written in one place, and where a query matches them.

kind.description: What the words are: a text, a description, notes, or a claim.

node.description: The node: the text's, or the one the description describes. None for notes or a claim.

beat.description: The beat, for its claim or its notes.

state.description:
The first state that shows them as written there: where `replace_text` is made. For
notes, the state they are of, or the beat's first; for a claim, the beat's first state.

states.description: Every state that shows them as written there, in the deck's order.

lives.description:
Where they are written, a JSON pointer into the deck: the node's own `text`, `runs`, or
`alt` (`/nodes/title/text`), a state's delta (`/states/2/props/title/text`), or the deck's
`overrides`, which hold it in every state (`/overrides/title/text`); a state's notes
(`/states/2/notes`); or a beat's claim or notes (`/spine/sections/0/beats/1/claim`).

text.description: The words: a text's `text`, or its runs' texts end to end.

matches.description:
Each match, `[from, to]` in characters (Unicode scalar values), as `replace_text`
counts them, in order; none overlap.

Kind.description: What words a match is in.

oneOf.description: A state's speaker notes, or a beat's.

Patched.description: What a patch did, or would do.

applied.description: Whether the deck was written: not under a dry run, nor when the patch was refused.

patch.description: The patch as RFC 6902, in order.

added.description: What `validate` and `lint` find after the patch that they did not before.

removed.description: What they found before that they do not after.

errors.description: The findings that are errors, after.

states.description:
The states it changes, by id: each whose nodes, resolved with the deck's overrides,
or whose layout, transition, choreography, hold, or notes are not as they were, and
each it adds. None when it is refused.

oneOf.description:
Put `value` at `path`: a member of an object (one already there is replaced, in its
place), or an item of an array, at an index or at its end (`-`).
Replace what is at `path`, which must be there.

`remove` at `from`, then `add` at `path`. A member moved within its object keeps its
place: a rename.
Fail the patch unless `path` holds `value` (numbers equal by value: 1 is 1.0).

Pointer.description:
A JSON Pointer (RFC 6901): empty, the whole document, or `/`-separated tokens, `~1` for a
`/` and `~0` for a `~` inside one.

Finding.description: One lint finding, shaped for agents: a code, a JSON pointer, and (when safe) a fix.

file.description: The bundle file `path` points into, when it is not `deck.json` (a theme file).

format.description: The format the deck was laid out in (`"9:16"`), when it is not the deck's own.

fix.description: A JSON Patch (RFC 6902) that resolves the finding. Only safe, non-content fixes.

found.description:
The words the query matches, once for each place they are written, in the order the
deck first shows them.

matches.description: The matches in all of them.

replaced.description:
With a replacement and a match: the one patch that replaces every match, a
`replace_text` for each in a text and a `replace` of other words, as `patch` reports it.
